transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical support, my name is Holly. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Holly. My broadband speed has dropped to less than ten megabits over the last week when I pay for Fibre 65, and every time the landline rings the internet disconnects completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating that must be, Sophia. Having your broadband drop out every time the phone rings makes the service almost unusable, and I will help get this resolved for you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Holly. My daughter was trying to do her university coursework and she kept getting thrown out of her lecture every time someone called me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we run line tests on your copper broadband, Sophia, could you please confirm your full installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 83 Millfield Road, York, YO23 1NQ, and the security PIN is 4172.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying your details, Sophia. I have your Fibre 65 VDSL line profile open in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, hopefully the line test shows something.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are experiencing: your download speeds have slumped down under ten megabits, and whenever an incoming telephone call arrives, your VDSL connection drops sync and drops off completely. Have I got that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly what's happening. The little broadband light on the router flashes orange whenever the landline phone rings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When broadband drops every time the telephone rings, it almost always points to high capacitance or bell-wire interference across internal extension wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bell-wire interference? What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In traditional UK homes, telephone extension sockets used a third wire on pin three designed to ring old mechanical bells. On modern VDSL broadband, that wire acts like a giant antenna picking up radio noise.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We do have three phone extension sockets around the house that were put in about twenty years ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where is your S-Net Hub router plugged in right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's plugged into an extension socket in the hallway near the stairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And where is the main master telephone socket where the line enters the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The main master socket is by the front door on the skirting board.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the master socket have a horizontal split across the middle of the plastic faceplate with two small screws?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... yes, it has a horizontal line across the middle and two screws on the bottom half. It says Openreach on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an NTE5 master socket. The bottom half contains the test socket behind it. When you unscrew the bottom faceplate, it completely disconnects all internal house extension wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I take those two screws out while on the phone with you?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Sophia. It is completely safe low-voltage wiring. Unscrew the two screws and gently pull the bottom faceplate forward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, unscrewing with a small coin... one screw out... second screw out... pulling the plate forward. Behind it on the right side there's another phone socket!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That hidden socket on the right is the engineer test socket. That connects directly to the street cable with zero internal wiring interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I plug the microfilter and router directly into that test socket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, please. Plug your microfilter directly into that test socket, and plug the gray broadband cable from your Hub into the ADSL/VDSL port on the filter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Plugging into the test socket now... and plugging the gray lead in... okay, the Hub is powering up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Watch the broadband light on the front of the Hub. It will flash orange while training, then should go solid white once synced.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's flashing orange... still flashing... and now it just turned solid white!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now I am going to call your landline telephone number from my test console to see if the Hub drops sync.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, calling now...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm ringing your number right now. Did your phone ring?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The phone plugged into the filter rang loud and clear, and the Hub light stayed completely solid white! It didn't drop at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms 100% that the line drop was caused by the bell-wire on your extension wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is incredible. What about the speed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On our copper telemetry, your SNR margin was forced up to twelve decibels by the exchange to stabilise the line, which capped your speed at eight megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can that speed cap be removed now that the noisy extension wiring is bypassed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can reset your DLM profile right now to target the optimal six decibel SNR margin.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please do, that would be wonderful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I reset your DLM line profile at the exchange to restore full speed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you very much for holding, Sophia. I have reset your Dynamic Line Management profile to remove the speed cap.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Holly. What speed should I be seeing now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you run a speed test on your phone or laptop on speedtest.net?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running speed test on my laptop... download is sixty-three megabits! And upload is eighteen megabits! I was only getting eight megabits before!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sixty-three megabits is the maximum sync rate for your line length from the cabinet, Sophia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My daughter will be over the moon. She can do all her university seminars without getting kicked out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To keep that full speed permanently, you can replace that older master faceplate with a modern filtered faceplate, which we will send you in the post tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the new filtered faceplate clip on with no screws?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it simply clips onto that master socket and automatically isolates the bell-wire so you can still use your hallway extension without speed loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will my telephone caller display still work through the filtered faceplate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, all telephone caller display and extension features will continue working with zero interference to the broadband.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And should I leave the router plugged into the master socket permanently?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, plugging directly into the master socket ensures the lowest possible attenuation and maximum stability.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also scheduled an automated 24-hour line health monitor on your circuit to confirm the speed remains stable at 63 megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That proactive check is really comforting.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Holly, you have been absolutely amazing today. You diagnosed the problem straight away and fixed it in minutes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm so delighted we could get your full Fibre 65 speed back and stop those telephone disconnects, Sophia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You've made my day, thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure. Is there anything else on your S-Net broadband that I can assist with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, everything is completely sorted. Thanks again Holly!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Sophia. Enjoy your fast broadband and have a lovely rest of your week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Holly, goodbye!
